walkthroughs.body_html: Yield (t/ha) = total harvest / area. A farm harvesting 60 tonnes of wheat from 8 hectares has 60/8 = 7.5 t/ha. UK wheat averages around 8 t/ha, among the highest globally. Closing the global yield gap sustainably is a key challenge: doubling food production by 2050 without expanding farmland or emissions.

Food miles measure distance from production to consumer. Air-freighted asparagus from Peru to UK travels around 10,000 km, while local seasonal produce may travel under 50 km. However, transport is often a small share of total emissions. Beef has high emissions regardless of distance, while seasonal local veg is usually low impact.

Producing 1 kg of beef takes around 15,000 L water, mostly to grow feed. Wheat needs around 1,800 L/kg, potatoes 290 L/kg and tomatoes 200 L/kg. Almond and rice production stress water-scarce regions. Switching diets toward plant-based foods can sharply cut water and carbon footprints, with co-benefits for biodiversity.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?
options: Stopping all development immediately.
Richness counts how many species exist; evenness measures how balanced their abundances are.
Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
They are the same measurement.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
Stopping all development immediately.
Environmental protection at all costs.
